title: Donut Emphasize — Static Per-Segment Highlight

complexity.rationale: Line already has a near-exact precedent for this exact mechanism: `primarySeries`/`otherSeriesColor` (packages/vega-spec-builder-s2/src/types/marks/lineSpec.types.ts:103-108, getStrokeEncoding in lineMarkUtils.ts:99-118, getPrimarySeriesOtherExpr in lineDataUtils.ts:64-69) - a static/data-driven test expression that swaps non-designated series to a gray color at full opacity, entirely independent of the opacity/hover system. Adapting it from series-level (SERIES_ID) to segment-level (idKey) grouping for the arc mark is a precedented, low-risk port. What keeps this at a 3 rather than a 2: donut's label treatment genuinely diverges from Line's (Line suppresses non-primary direct labels entirely; the Figma reference shows donut keeps non-emphasized labels fully visible, just plainer), and there's a real open question about interaction with donut-hover and whether to literally reuse the highlightedItem/primarySeries naming or introduce a donut-specific prop.

summary: Emphasize is a not-yet-built, static/data-driven (not mouse-driven) per-segment highlight: the emphasized segment(s) keep full categorical color, while all other segments render as a solid color swap to secondary-gray (#C6C6C6/gray-400) at full opacity - not a fade. Confirmed via a live 6-segment Figma example: exactly one segment (North America) stays in full indigo color with an Advanced Label (swatch+name+value+detail+connector), while the other five segments render solid gray with plain Direct Labels (name+percent only) at full, undimmed opacity. This is functionally very close to Line's existing `primarySeries`/`otherSeriesColor` feature, just applied per-segment instead of per-series.
requirements: The emphasized segment's arc keeps its full categorical color and full opacity, unchanged.

All non-emphasized segments' arcs render as a solid color swap to secondary-gray (gray-400/#C6C6C6), at full opacity - not a fade/reduced-opacity treatment. This must be a distinct mechanism from both donut-hover's opacity fade (FADE_FACTOR=0.2) and the existing generic highlightedItem/CONTROLLED_HIGHLIGHTED_ITEM opacity-fade used elsewhere - confirmed visually (non-emphasized segments in the Figma reference are fully opaque solid gray, not semi-transparent).

Non-emphasized segments' labels (direct or advanced) render at full, normal opacity and their normal colors - unlike Line's primarySeries (which suppresses non-primary direct labels entirely), donut's non-emphasized labels stay visible, just not necessarily in the richer Advanced Label style. Confirmed visually (EMEA/APAC/LATAM/Japan/Others direct labels all render at full gray-700 opacity, undimmed, in the reference).

Direct labels and advanced labels can be freely combined on the same chart when using emphasize - e.g. an AdvancedLabel on the emphasized segment paired with plain SegmentLabels on the rest, as shown in the reference - but this pairing is not a hard requirement of emphasize itself; which label type appears on which segment is an independent, orthogonal authoring choice (a user could equally emphasize a segment that only has a plain SegmentLabel, or none at all).

Reuse the precedented shape of Line's `primarySeries`/`otherSeriesColor` mechanism (a static test-expression-driven color swap, fully independent of opacity/hover) rather than building something new from scratch - adapted from series-level grouping to segment-level (per-arc, keyed by idKey) grouping. See openQuestions for whether the donut-facing prop should reuse `highlightedItem` or introduce its own name.

Support at least one emphasized segment; confirm whether multiple segments can be emphasized simultaneously - Line's `primarySeries` already supports either a count (`number`) or a named list (`string[]`), and DonutSpecOptions' existing (currently unwired) `highlightedItem` type also already supports an array, suggesting multi-select is the expected shape either way.

designTokens.usage: Fill for non-emphasized segments - exact match for Line's existing default otherSeriesColor fallback ('gray-400'), confirmed visually against the Figma reference.
The emphasize reference example uses exactly 6 segments (North America, EMEA, APAC, LATAM, Japan, Others), consistent with donut-chart-tokens' documented maxSegments cap.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: RESOLVED: emphasize has no effect at all on boolean donuts - getArcFillEncoding (donutUtils.ts) gives isBoolean's own secondary-gray treatment full precedence (`if (!isBoolean) return getEmphasizeFillEncoding(options);`), so emphasizedItems is silently ignored rather than combined or conflicting. Confirmed by code inspection; not currently covered by an explicit regression test.

edgeCases.case: Hovering a non-emphasized (grayed-out) segment (interaction with donut-hover)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: v1 decision (tentative, not locked in): hover is suppressed entirely while any segment is emphasized - HOVERED_ITEM is forced to null via addHoveredItemSignal's excludeCondition (donutSpecBuilder.ts addSignals) whenever emphasizedItems is non-empty, so no segment fades/highlights on hover and no label color-switches. This was a deliberate simplification for the first iteration, not a confirmed final design - revisit whether non-emphasized segments should remain independently hoverable (e.g. temporarily restoring full color/opacity) in a follow-up iteration.

edgeCases.case: Hovering a non-emphasized segment's direct/advanced label value (interaction with donut-hover/donut-advanced-labels' hover-color-switch)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Resolved by the same v1 blanket suppression above: since HOVERED_ITEM is forced to null whenever emphasizedItems is non-empty, no label's value line ever color-switches on hover while emphasize is active. Revisit alongside the hover-suppression decision if that changes.
All segments render in full color as today - this feature must be fully opt-in with no visual change when unused.

RESOLVED: correctly degenerates to identical-to-'no emphasize' - getEmphasizeOtherExpr's `indexof(emphasizedItems, datum.color) < 0` test is false for every row when every color is in the list, so no segment ever gets the gray swap.

edgeCases.case: Donut paired with a `<Legend>` (interaction with donut-hover's legend-sync work)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: RESOLVED: legend sync stays scoped to real mouse hover only - emphasize does not touch legendHighlightSignals or the arc's opacity encode at all (only the static fill), and touchesLegendInteraction is correctly false. A non-emphasized (grayed) segment's Legend entry is unaffected by emphasize; it only reacts to actual hover, consistent with donut-hover's existing behavior.

crossCutting.notes: touchesHoverAnimation: real open interaction question with donut-hover (see edgeCases) that must be resolved before/during implementation, not left implicit. touchesControlledHighlight: this feature IS the concrete realization of the 'controlled highlight' concept for donut - DonutSpecOptions already declares a `highlightedItem` field (donutSpec.types.ts) that is not currently consumed anywhere in donutSpecBuilder.ts/donutUtils.ts's actual logic (only appears in the destructured type union), so this spec should decide whether emphasize wires up that existing-but-dormant field or introduces a new one - see openQuestions. touchesTooltipOrPopover: false - emphasize is a static prop unrelated to the isInteractive/popover gate, unlike donut-hover. requiresNewSignalOrScale: true - needs a new (or newly-wired) test-expression-driven fill rule on the arc mark, adapted from Line's getPrimarySeriesOtherExpr pattern rather than built from scratch. requiresS1S2Parity is false: there is no existing s1 'emphasize' implementation to mirror (Line's primarySeries is the precedent this feature adapts, not an existing donut s1 feature), so this is s2-only work by definition, not a parity gap.

implementationPlan.change: In getArcMark (lines 48-76), add a fill production rule that swaps non-emphasized segments to secondary-gray (gray-400) at full opacity, adapted from Line's getStrokeEncoding/getPrimarySeriesOtherExpr pattern (test expression checking whether the segment's idKey is in the emphasized set, gray otherwise) - keep this fully separate from the existing getMarkOpacity opacity encode, since this is a color swap, not an opacity change.
Reference only - getPrimarySeriesOtherExpr (lines 64-69) is the pattern to adapt: swap SERIES_ID/color-domain-slice logic for donut's idKey-based per-segment equivalent.
Added new `emphasizedItems?: (string | number)[]` and `otherItemColor?: string` fields to DonutOptions - did not wire up the existing `highlightedItem` field, which remains dormant.

Threaded emphasizedItems through addDonut's produce callback into donutOptions; also added the excludeCondition wiring on addHoveredItemSignal that suppresses hover entirely while emphasizedItems is non-empty (see edgeCases).
Added a regression test confirming label encodes are untouched by the emphasize field, per requirement 3. advancedLabelUtils.ts wasn't touched since donut-advanced-labels doesn't exist yet.
ADDED (not in original plan): companion test coverage for the emphasize fill encoding and the hover-suppression signal wiring.

CORRECTED PATH (originally planned as components/Donut or SegmentLabel/AdvancedLabel story files): added Basic (single emphasized segment) and Multi (multiple emphasized segments) stories - not the full 6-segment AdvancedLabel Figma reference scenario, since donut-advanced-labels doesn't exist yet.

openQuestions: RESOLVED: introduced entirely new donut-specific props - `emphasizedItems?: (string | number)[]` and `otherItemColor?: string` (DonutOptions/DonutSpecOptions) - rather than reusing the existing (still-unwired) `highlightedItem` field or literally mirroring Line's `primarySeries`/`otherSeriesColor` names. `highlightedItem` remains dormant/unconsumed, unaffected by this feature.

RESOLVED for v1 (tentatively): hover is suppressed entirely while any segment is emphasized, rather than allowing non-emphasized segments to remain independently hoverable. This was the simplest first-iteration behavior, not a confirmed final design - open follow-up question: should non-emphasized segments regain their own hover/fade behavior (independent of the emphasized segment's static gray state) in a later iteration? See edgeCases.
RESOLVED: yes - `emphasizedItems` is typed as an array (`(string | number)[]`), so multiple segments can be emphasized simultaneously, matching Line's primarySeries flexibility.
